newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek tax revenues up 14.2 pct in February- finmin.
newsitem.headline: Greek tax revenues up 14.2 pct in February- finmin.

text.p: Greece's central government tax revenues were growing by 14.2 percent in February, slightly below the projected growth rate of 14.6 percent in this year's budget, Deputy Finance Minister George Drys said in an inteview.
Drys was speaking to Flash radio station.
Greece's general government budget deficit is projected at 4.2 percent of GDP in 1997 compared with an estimated 7.6 percent of GDP in 1996.
General government tax revenues are forecast to grow by 14.9 percent and current spending by 5.8 percent in 1997.

The central government's budget deficit is projected at 6.2 percent of GDP in 1997 against an estimated 9.3 percent in 1996. Central government tax revenues are forecast to grow by 14.6 percent and current spending by 4.9 percent in 1997.
